notes: RBox revision of the topic's symmetry property (RBOX_PER_TOPIC: symmetry). mutualist_of is catalogued symmetric; the edit flips it to asymmetric, as the template flips twinning. The earlier version made 'is a parasite of' symmetric, which two reviews rejected: parasitism is at the host's expense by definition, so the edited world made frogs and crabs parasites of their parasites and clashed with class-level knowledge, and the original property (asymmetry) is one the dataset does not use as a stored property. Mutualism has no such class-level conflict: a partnership that is reciprocal in ordinary biology is the property being revised, as with twinning. The instances are minor pairs given by binomial names (the yucca moth Tegeticula yuccasella with Yucca filamentosa; the ant Pseudomyrmex ferrugineus with the bull's-horn acacia Acacia cornigera), so no famous reciprocal pair (clownfish and anemones) lets a stored converse decide the answer. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the direct question asks 'asymmetric' (no, then yes), the first instance asks whether the converse follows (yes, then no), the second whether the fact rules the converse out (no, then yes). The cross-lingual queries ask the first instance with a directed 'is a mutualist of' wording (Chinese 互利共生者, Spanish 'mutualista de') and keep the Latin names. Near unrelated asks the same property of another relation ('is a sibling of' is not asymmetric: a leak turns no to yes); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge (1 + 1), as the other RBox records do. Evidence: infini-gram counts only; Wikipedia answered HTTP 429, so no quotes and no exact-phrase counts of 100 or more are given for the two pair facts.

Tegeticula yuccasella is a mutualist of.why: True: the yucca moth Tegeticula yuccasella is a pollinator of Yucca filamentosa and its larvae feed on the seeds, the textbook obligate pollination mutualism.
